question: Should `agents.defaults.sandbox.mode: "needed"` cover Codex app-server native shell/files/process/MCP surfaces, or should the public contract be narrowed before merge?
rationale: This PR adds a public sandbox/config value and changes when OpenClaw requires a sandbox backend, so the permanent fail-closed boundary needs maintainer security intent rather than an implicit contributor choice.

options.title: Complete Needed Across Native Execution
options.body: Keep the public mode and require Codex-native execution to lazy-resolve the OpenClaw sandbox or fail closed before exposing shell/files/process/MCP work.

options.title: Narrow The Public Contract
options.body: Document and enforce `needed` only for embedded OpenClaw exec while disabling or excluding Codex-native surfaces until a separate design lands.

options.title: Pause Or Close The Direction
options.body: Leave the draft paused if maintainers do not want another sandbox mode in core without a broader sandbox placement design.

recommendation.title: Complete Needed Across Native Execution
recommendation.body: Keep the public mode and require Codex-native execution to lazy-resolve the OpenClaw sandbox or fail closed before exposing shell/files/process/MCP work.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined signal from sandbox architecture history and prior security-boundary routing.
